newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA's Fraser says rate cut depends on economy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA's Fraser says rate cut depends on economy.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Bernie Fraser said on Thursday that the central bank would cut official rates again if the economy needed support.

Fraser, in an address to a parliamentary committee, also said he would want to see a comfortable inflation outlook before another rate cut was considered. The RBA last cut the official rate in July by 50 basis points to 7.0 percent.
"It is the trends in the domestic economy that are most important in leading to adjustments to monetary policy," Fraser said.
In response to a question from former Labor Treasurer Ralph Willis, who asked if another rate cut would be based on the RBA's view that the economy needed support, Fraser said:
"Yes, that's right and if that could be accommodated in a situation where inflation was declining and the outlook for inflation was comfortable."
Specifically, Willis had asked -- "If there were to be any further reductions in interest rates, that would be because the bank would feel that the economy needed more support to maintain growth?"
Fraser said the RBA constantly made assessments of what was happening to the economy, including employment and unemployment as well as inflation.
"We are a bit more confident about what might happen on inflation over the next six or 12 months than we are about what might happen to growth and employment."
